Selective breeding involves choosing parents with particular characteristics to breed with each other to produce offspring with more desirable characteristics. The two types of selective breeding/artificial selection are:

audio_hyperlinks.explanation: The process by which humans breed animals and plants for particular desired traits.

reading_flow.text: Inbreeding: is the process of producing offspring through mating genetically similar organisms. After many generations of inbreeding, the offspring will be almost genetically identical and will produce identical offspring. When this happens, an organism is described as inbred or purebred. Pure breeds are animals with homogeneous appearance, behavior and other characteristics. Purebred breeding aims to establish and maintain stable traits that the animal can pass on to the next generation that could help to develop superior qualities. The negative consequence of inbreeding is that it makes the expression of undesired recessive traits in the family more likely.

audio_hyperlinks.explanation: Mating between closely related organisms, leading to increased genetic uniformity.
An organism with parents of the same breed or variety, possessing stable and uniform traits.

reading_flow.text: Crossbreeding: is the process of producing offspring through mating two purebred individuals that come from different breeds, varieties, or even species. Crossbreeding involves breeding two unrelated individuals. For instance, crossbreeding of the local breeds with exotic sires. Crossbreeding is incompatible with the conservation of indigenous breeds.

audio_hyperlinks.explanation: Mating individuals from different breeds, varieties, or species to combine desirable traits.

reading_flow.text: Figure 4.38 shows examples of selective breeding of sheep with long tails, with long horn sheep and wheat and Borena cattle and Camel breeds in Ethiopia.

On the other hand, natural selection is the selection of certain traits without any human intervention. Plants and animals that are better adapted to their environment have a higher chance of survival and producing more offspring than less adapted plants and animals.

audio_hyperlinks.explanation: The process whereby organisms better adapted to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring.
